data.title: bn-3o5q: Build trusted cold-trial fixture preparation seam

data.body:
[HIGH] Recovery can certify a partial or corrupt protected preparation as settled. can_settle() checks only the filename set. On reopen, load_existing() hashes whatever bytes exist (lines 542-603) but, for a pending transaction, never decodes or cross-validates reset/target/session/accounting/preparation receipts. write_bytes() creates the final filename before write_all/fsync (lines 618-657), so a SIGKILL or short/erroring final preparation.json write can leave all 17 expected names. A retry with the still-live supervisor then publishes the workspace, writes settlement.json over those re-baselined bytes, and reports preparation.settled=true. The existing complete_pending_and_settled_transactions_recover_idempotently test (lines 1001-1022) demonstrates the issue by settling arbitrary filename bytes. Make each artifact publication atomic (private temp file, fsync, no-replace rename, directory fsync), and validate the complete typed receipt graph and all referenced digests/identities/counters before can_settle becomes true.

risk:high failure-mode checklist: 1) Failure modes: process death, ENOSPC/short write, or durability failure after final-name creation can turn incomplete evidence into a settled receipt. 2) Edge cases: inject faults after create, during write, after file fsync, before/after directory fsync, and restart with a live supervisor; corrupt each cross-reference and original independently. 3) Rollback: stop the authenticated runtime, quarantine the referee directory, and prepare a new workspace/root; never grade or reuse the suspect transaction. 4) Monitoring/alerts: expose a typed pending-invalid/recovery-refused state and require the grader to observe a fully validated settlement before grading. 5) Input validation: on reopen strictly decode every receipt, reject unknown/duplicate/missing entries, recompute all file refs/digests, enforce session/cookie/subject and accounting invariants, and only then permit settlement.

[MEDIUM] The settlement transition has an unrecoverable crash window. workspace.json is installed first, then settlement.json is installed separately. If the process dies after the first write, load_existing() classifies the transaction as Pending because settlement.json is absent, while can_settle() requires a pending transaction to contain exactly PREPARED_ARTIFACTS and therefore rejects the extra workspace.json. resume() then stops the matching runtime as incomplete; no retry path can validate and finish this otherwise complete preparation. Model the pre-settlement workspace receipt as an explicit recoverable state (and validate it against the inode-bound workspace), or atomically publish a transaction state that lets restart deterministically finish/roll back. Add a fault-injection regression for death after workspace.json durability and before settlement.json publication.

data.reason: Protected preparation recovery is not fail-closed: a final-name partial artifact can be re-baselined and settled, and a crash after workspace.json leaves a complete preparation permanently unrecoverable. See th-227luc and th-2pli5t.

data.body: Fixed in d4ac0b0: protected artifacts now use private 0600 temp files, staged write fault points, file fsync, renameat2 NOREPLACE, and directory fsync; interrupted temps/finals are retained but never adopted. Recovery strictly decodes deny-unknown typed receipts with duplicate-safe wire decoding and cross-validates the transaction/root/workspace identities, exact binary pins, reset/target, declaration/pass/canonical manifest/history, every FileRef digest/size/path, all seven response originals/session/subject/cookie relations, and accounting invariants before can_settle. Regressions cover each publication crash stage, racing final names, malformed/truncated/duplicate/unknown receipts, and independent corruption of every prepared artifact. Focused tests, exact pinned two-mode native qualification, and RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 just check pass; native log sha256 2a3816c9fc143ecec1879ef09068e28986ccbd205433c8680ae68c9d046c8299, full-check log sha256 8cb0fa0b282c28343ee33c6ec2c956dd36d695706f01836135af166a7114e96a.

Fixed in d4ac0b0: workspace.json now transitions to an explicit PreSettlement state only after atomic durable publication, and its receipt is bound to the captured workspace dev+ino and revalidated before/after inventory. Restart recognizes exactly prepared+workspace, validates the full graph and current inode-bound workspace, then deterministically finishes settlement; workspace substitution fails closed and retains evidence. Added crash_after_workspace_receipt_recovers_and_finishes_settlement plus same-content inode-replacement refusal regressions. Focused tests, exact pinned two-mode native qualification, and RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 just check pass; native log sha256 2a3816c9fc143ecec1879ef09068e28986ccbd205433c8680ae68c9d046c8299, full-check log sha256 8cb0fa0b282c28343ee33c6ec2c956dd36d695706f01836135af166a7114e96a.

Verified at d4ac0b0e83b28c2dd285236ef4fc2bfcaf727b05. write_bytes_with (preparation.rs:963-1023) uses a private 0600 O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW temp, complete write, file sync, renameat2 NOREPLACE, directory sync, held inode/digest registration, and post-publication verification. Recovery classifies only the exact pending/pre-settlement/settled name sets (615-641), strictly decodes duplicate-safe deny-unknown receipts, and validates the transaction, pins, reset/target, canonical declaration/pass/manifest/history, every FileRef and identity original, session/cookie/subject relations, accounting, workspace, and settlement before can_settle succeeds (644-936). The atomic stage/race and every-artifact/receipt-corruption regressions passed; exact native and full serial gates also passed. Fix satisfies this finding.

Verified at d4ac0b0e83b28c2dd285236ef4fc2bfcaf727b05. TransactionState::PreSettlement is classified only for the exact prepared plus workspace.json set (preparation.rs:627-633). settle_with durably publishes workspace.json, records the explicit state, and on retry revalidates the full prepared graph, the transaction-captured workspace dev+ino before and after recursive inventory, and the saved workspace receipt before writing settlement.json (517-582, 644-671, 882-915). crash_after_workspace_receipt_recovers_and_finishes_settlement and the same-content inode-replacement refusal both passed. Fix satisfies this finding.
